answer: Registration costs a bond. A new agent locks 50,000 POA in escrow to vote, and every attestation it casts burns a slice of that bond; when a non-kin jury later marks the vote false, the rest is slashed into the pool. A fleet of 5,000 fake identities must lock 250,000,000 POA at once, and every wrong vote spends real stake rather than nothing. The bond frees after 30 votes, so an attacker buys a month of patience per identity or funds the fleet outright. Each identity is an island reached by one jetty, and the bond is the lantern: no lantern, no mooring.
